outlook_findings.passage: **CET1 rebuild against RWA growth** — a further decline from 14.1% alongside continued RWA expansion would tighten the capital deployment story [claim-005][claim-006].
outlook_findings.evidence: This, and the section 4 heading "**Capital was consumed, not accumulated.**", present the quarter's capital picture one-sidedly. claims.json contains management's own directly contrary position, which the brief never cites anywhere: claim-043 records the CEO saying excess capital is still approximately $40 billion and that the firm now thinks it could actually deploy it over time, and claim-044 records the stated goal of deploying capital at a 17% return. On management's account the CET1 decline is deliberate deployment into client growth, not a constraint tightening. claim-046 (an analyst challenging the buyback at 3 times tangible book) is also available and unused. The remit treats an available claim that cuts the other way as a real finding, and this is the clearest instance in the run.
outlook_findings.recommendation: In section 4 or section 8, state management's $40 billion excess-capital and 17% deployment-return position with citations to claim-043 and claim-044, and frame the CET1 decline against it, so the monitor item reads as a two-sided test rather than a one-sided concern.

outlook_findings.passage: Investment banking fees, which grew more slowly than the trading line this quarter [claim-012][claim-016], have more headroom precisely because they were not at peak;
outlook_findings.evidence: This is the load-bearing mechanism of the entire upside case, and it is stated as fact with "precisely because". The two cited claims do not establish it. claim-012 says only that IB fees rose 30% year-on-year; claim-016 says only that equities revenue rose 86%. A lower growth rate does not establish that the absolute fee level is below peak. The proposition happens to be true in the source (seg-0008: "by historical standards, investment banking fees were fine, but they weren't at sort of super peak levels. So, they had some room to come up a little bit"), but no claim in claims.json captures that sentence, so a reader auditing the citation trail cannot verify the premise. The citations resolve while not supporting the sentence they sit under.
outlook_findings.recommendation: Either extract a new claim for the "not at super peak levels" statement in seg-0003/seg-0008 and cite it here, or rewrite the clause as an explicitly authorial inference from the growth-rate gap rather than a causal fact.

outlook_findings.passage: The firm also increased the equity allocation to the CIB during the quarter [claim-053].
outlook_findings.evidence: This sentence closes the section 4 paragraph headed "**Capital was consumed, not accumulated.**", which places it in the capital-depletion narrative. Read in seg-0021, the equity allocation change is an internal reallocation from Corporate into the CIB, explicitly described by the speaker as moving equity between pockets of the same firm. It consumes no group capital and is not evidence for the paragraph's thesis.
outlook_findings.recommendation: Move the sentence out of the capital-consumption paragraph, or add a clause noting it is an internal reallocation rather than a group capital outflow.

outlook_findings.passage: if rates stay higher, the deposit convexity management warned about could force a repricing of the franchise [claim-038]
outlook_findings.evidence: claim-038 and its segment (seg-0041) set a materially higher trigger than "rates stay higher". The speaker frames the convexity risk around "something that's like meaningfully different, that's a true stress test with an actual change in regime", and illustrates it with a 7% rate environment; he also says the effect has not yet appeared in this cycle. The brief's own section 8 states the condition correctly ("the convexity effect management said has not yet appeared but must eventually"), so the section 7 wording is an internal inconsistency as well as a softening of the stated threshold.
outlook_findings.recommendation: Align the section 7 condition with section 8 and with claim-038's own framing, e.g. "if rates move to a meaningfully higher regime rather than merely staying elevated".

outlook_findings.passage: trivial for the full year on management's own account, but forecast to accelerate meaningfully in the second half and named as an important question for next year [claim-048]
outlook_findings.evidence: The first two limbs are supported by claim-048's quote. The third, "named as an important question for next year", is not in that quote; it comes from a later sentence of seg-0101 ("it is an important question for us as we go into next year") that was not extracted. The brief also omits the speaker's explicit disclaimer in the same segment that token expense "is not in any way a meaningful driver of the current outlook or to the revision in the outlook", which matters because this is promoted to one of eight monitor items.
outlook_findings.recommendation: Extract the "important question for next year" sentence as its own claim and cite it, or drop the clause; and add management's not-a-meaningful-driver qualifier to the bullet.

summary: Two medium findings, both in outlook-brief.md. First, the brief reads the quarter's capital position one-sidedly: it heads a section "Capital was consumed, not accumulated" and makes CET1 rebuild a monitor item, while never citing claim-043 and claim-044, in which management states it still has roughly $40 billion of excess capital and intends to deploy it at a 17% return. Second, the upside case rests on the premise that investment banking fees "were not at peak", cited to claim-012 and claim-016, neither of which establishes that; the supporting statement exists in seg-0008 but was never extracted as a claim. Four low findings concern qualifiers dropped between transcript and brief (claim-054's materiality, claim-038's regime-change threshold, claim-048's not-a-meaningful-driver disclaimer) and claim-053 being placed inside a capital-consumption paragraph although it describes an internal reallocation. Against that, the run is strong where it matters most: every claim-### citation in the brief resolves to the correct claim, the exhaustive numeric semantic review over all 44 value-bearing claims found no operand, unit, sign or period error, the (sic) "Including/Excluding" transcript correction was handled correctly and is corroborated by the SEC 10-Q facts, and the temporal-integrity guard worked, excluding two post-event web captures that provider metadata had mislabelled pre_event. Both deterministic gates passed with zero issues across two attempts and the injection scan is clean. The run can proceed with the warnings surfaced.
